balance_transaction_fee_details.name: amount
balance_transaction_fee_details.comment: Amount of the fee, in cents.

balance_transaction_fee_details.name: application
balance_transaction_fee_details.comment: ID of the Connect application that earned the fee.

balance_transaction_fee_details.name: batch_timestamp
balance_transaction_fee_details.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

balance_transaction_fee_details.name: currency
balance_transaction_fee_details.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

balance_transaction_fee_details.name: description
balance_transaction_fee_details.comment: An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.

balance_transaction_fee_details.name: type
balance_transaction_fee_details.comment: Type of the fee, one of: application_fee, payment_method_passthrough_fee, stripe_fee, tax, or withheld_tax.

balance_transactions.name: amount
balance_transactions.comment: Gross amount of this transaction (in cents). A positive value represents funds charged to another party, and a negative value represents funds sent to another party.

balance_transactions.name: automatic_transfer_id
balance_transactions.comment: ID of the automatically created transfer associated with this balance transaction (only set if your account is on an automatic payout schedule).

balance_transactions.name: available_on
balance_transactions.comment: The date that the transaction's net funds become available in the Stripe balance.

balance_transactions.name: batch_timestamp
balance_transactions.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

balance_transactions.name: created
balance_transactions.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

balance_transactions.name: currency
balance_transactions.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

balance_transactions.name: description
balance_transactions.comment: An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.

balance_transactions.name: exchange_rate
balance_transactions.comment:
This field is populated for Balance Transactions created beyond January 26th, 2026.

If applicable, the exchange rate used on this Balance Transaction. Divide the amount of the transaction by this rate to determine the amount in the original currency. For example, consider a Balance Transaction that has an amount of 1234 and an exchange_rate of 1.234. The original amount would then be equal to 1234 / 1.234 = 1000.

balance_transactions.name: fee
balance_transactions.comment: Fees (in cents) paid for this transaction. Represented as a positive integer when assessed.

balance_transactions.name: net
balance_transactions.comment: Net impact to a Stripe balance (in cents). A positive value represents incrementing a Stripe balance, and a negative value decrementing a Stripe balance. You can calculate the net impact of a transaction on a balance by amount - fee

balance_transactions.name: reporting_category
balance_transactions.comment: A new categorization of balance transactions, meant to improve on the current type field. Learn more. Please let us know what would be most helpful using the Feedback link at the bottom of this page.

balance_transactions.name: source_id
balance_transactions.comment: This transaction relates to the Stripe object.

balance_transactions.name: status
balance_transactions.comment: The transaction's net funds status in the Stripe balance, which are either available or pending.

balance_transactions.name: type
balance_transactions.comment: Transaction type: tax_fund, adjustment, advance, advance_funding, anticipation_repayment, application_fee, application_fee_refund, charge, climate_order_purchase, climate_order_refund, connect_collection_transfer, contribution, inbound_transfer, inbound_transfer_reversal, issuing_authorization_hold, issuing_authorization_release, issuing_dispute, issuing_transaction, obligation_outbound, obligation_reversal_inbound, payment, payment_failure_refund, payment_network_reserve_hold, payment_network_reserve_release, payment_refund, payment_reversal, payment_unreconciled, payout, payout_cancel, payout_failure, payout_minimum_balance_hold, payout_minimum_balance_release, refund, refund_failure, reserve_transaction, reserved_funds, reserve_hold, reserve_release, stripe_fee, stripe_fx_fee, stripe_balance_payment_debit, stripe_balance_payment_debit_reversal, tax_fee, topup, topup_reversal, transfer, transfer_cancel, transfer_failure, transfer_refund, or fee_credit_funding. Learn more about balance transaction types and what they represent. To classify transactions for accounting purposes, consider reporting_category instead.

charges.name: id
charges.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

charges.name: amount
charges.comment: Amount intended to be collected by this payment. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or equivalent in charge currency. The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).

charges.name: amount_refunded
charges.comment: Amount in cents refunded (can be less than the amount attribute on the charge if a partial refund was issued).

charges.name: application_fee_id
charges.comment: The application fee (if any) for the charge. See the Connect documentation for details.

charges.name: application_id
charges.comment: ID of the Connect application that created the charge.

charges.name: balance_transaction_id
charges.comment: ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this charge on your account balance (not including refunds or disputes).

charges.name: batch_timestamp
charges.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

charges.name: calculated_statement_descriptor
charges.comment: The full statement descriptor that is passed to card networks, and that is displayed on your customers' credit card and bank statements. Allows you to see what the statement descriptor looks like after the static and dynamic portions are combined. This value only exists for card payments.

charges.name: captured
charges.comment: If the charge was created without capturing, this Boolean represents whether it is still uncaptured or has since been captured.

charges.name: card_address_city
charges.comment: City/District/Suburb/Town/Village.

charges.name: card_address_country
charges.comment: Billing address country, if provided when creating card.

charges.name: card_address_line1
charges.comment: Address line 1 (Street address/PO Box/Company name).

charges.name: card_address_line1_check
charges.comment: If address_line1 was provided, results of the check: pass, fail, unavailable, or unchecked.

charges.name: card_address_line2
charges.comment: Address line 2 (Apartment/Suite/Unit/Building).

charges.name: card_address_state
charges.comment: State/County/Province/Region.

charges.name: card_address_zip
charges.comment: ZIP or postal code.

charges.name: card_address_zip_check
charges.comment: If address_zip was provided, results of the check: pass, fail, unavailable, or unchecked.

charges.name: card_brand
charges.comment: Card brand. Can be American Express, Cartes Bancaires, Diners Club, Discover, Eftpos Australia, Girocard, JCB, MasterCard, UnionPay, Visa, or Unknown.

charges.name: card_country
charges.comment: Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.

charges.name: card_customer_id
charges.comment: The customer that this card belongs to. This attribute will not be in the card object if the card belongs to an account or recipient instead.

charges.name: card_cvc_check
charges.comment: If a CVC was provided, results of the check: pass, fail, unavailable, or unchecked. A result of unchecked indicates that CVC was provided but hasn't been checked yet. Checks are typically performed when attaching a card to a Customer object, or when creating a charge. For more details, see Check if a card is valid without a charge.

charges.name: card_default_for_currency
charges.comment: Only applicable on payout external account card belonging to merchant (not as payment source customer card in charge).

charges.name: card_dynamic_last4
charges.comment: (For tokenized numbers only.) The last four digits of the device account number.

charges.name: card_exp_month
charges.comment: Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.

charges.name: card_exp_year
charges.comment: Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.

charges.name: card_fingerprint
charges.comment:
Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.

As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.

charges.name: card_funding
charges.comment: Card funding type. Can be credit, debit, prepaid, or unknown.

charges.name: card_id
charges.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

charges.name: card_last4
charges.comment: The last four digits of the card.

charges.name: card_name
charges.comment: Cardholder name.

charges.name: card_network
charges.comment: Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be amex, cartes_bancaires, diners, discover, eftpos_au, interac, jcb, link, mastercard, unionpay, visa, or unknown.

charges.name: card_token_type
charges.comment: If the card number is tokenized, this is the token type. For Apple Pay it can be dpan, mpan. For Google Pay Gateway integration it can be pan, dpan, ecommerce_token, pan_with_3ds. For Google Pay legacy integration it can be fpan, dpan_or_ecommerce_token.

charges.name: card_tokenization_method
charges.comment: If the card number is tokenized, this is the method that was used. Can be android_pay (includes Google Pay), apple_pay, masterpass, visa_checkout, or null.

charges.name: created
charges.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

charges.name: currency
charges.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

charges.name: customer_id
charges.comment: ID of the customer this charge is for if one exists.

charges.name: description
charges.comment: An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.

charges.name: failure_code
charges.comment: Error code explaining reason for charge failure if available (see the errors section for a list of codes).

charges.name: failure_message
charges.comment: Message to user further explaining reason for charge failure if available.

charges.name: invoice_id
charges.comment: ID of the invoice this charge is for if one exists.

charges.name: on_behalf_of_id
charges.comment: The account (if any) the charge was made on behalf of without triggering an automatic transfer. See the Connect documentation for details.

charges.name: outcome_advice_code
charges.comment: An enumerated value providing a more detailed explanation on how to proceed with an error.

charges.name: outcome_network_advice_code
charges.comment: For charges declined by the network, a 2 digit code which indicates the advice returned by the network on how to proceed with an error.

charges.name: outcome_network_decline_code
charges.comment: For charges declined by the network, an alphanumeric code which indicates the reason the charge failed.

charges.name: outcome_network_status
charges.comment: Possible values are approved_by_network, declined_by_network, not_sent_to_network, and reversed_after_approval. The value reversed_after_approval indicates the payment was blocked by Stripe after bank authorization, and may temporarily appear as "pending" on a cardholder's statement.

charges.name: outcome_reason
charges.comment: An enumerated value providing a more detailed explanation of the outcome's type. Charges blocked by Radar's default block rule have the value highest_risk_level. Charges placed in review by Radar's default review rule have the value elevated_risk_level. Charges blocked because the payment is unlikely to be authorized have the value low_probability_of_authorization. Charges authorized, blocked, or placed in review by custom rules have the value rule. See understanding declines for more details.

charges.name: outcome_rule_id
charges.comment: The ID of the Radar rule that matched the payment, if applicable.

charges.name: outcome_seller_message
charges.comment: A human-readable description of the outcome type and reason, designed for you (the recipient of the payment), not your customer.

charges.name: outcome_type
charges.comment: Possible values are authorized, manual_review, issuer_declined, blocked, and invalid. See understanding declines and Radar reviews for details.

charges.name: paid
charges.comment: true if the charge succeeded, or was successfully authorized for later capture.

charges.name: payment_intent
charges.comment: ID of the PaymentIntent associated with this charge, if one exists.

charges.name: payment_method_id
charges.comment: ID of the payment method used in this charge.

charges.name: payment_method_type
charges.comment: The type of transaction-specific details of the payment method used in the payment. See PaymentMethod.type for the full list of possible types. An additional hash is included on payment_method_details with a name matching this value. It contains information specific to the payment method.

charges.name: presentment_amount
charges.comment: Amount intended to be collected by this payment, denominated in presentment_currency.

charges.name: presentment_currency
charges.comment: Currency presented to the customer during payment.

charges.name: receipt_email
charges.comment: This is the email address that the receipt for this charge was sent to.

charges.name: receipt_number
charges.comment: This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this charge. This attribute will be null until a receipt has been sent.

charges.name: refunded
charges.comment: Whether the charge has been fully refunded. If the charge is only partially refunded, this attribute will still be false.

charges.name: shipping_address_city
charges.comment: City, district, suburb, town, or village.

charges.name: shipping_address_country
charges.comment: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

charges.name: shipping_address_line1
charges.comment: Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.

charges.name: shipping_address_line2
charges.comment: Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

charges.name: shipping_address_postal_code
charges.comment: ZIP or postal code.

charges.name: shipping_address_state
charges.comment: State, county, province, or region (ISO 3166-2).

charges.name: source_transfer_id
charges.comment: The transfer ID which created this charge. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account. See the Connect documentation for details.

charges.name: statement_descriptor
charges.comment:
For a non-card charge, text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see the Statement Descriptor docs.

For a card charge, this value is ignored unless you don't specify a statement_descriptor_suffix, in which case this value is used as the suffix.

charges.name: statement_descriptor_suffix
charges.comment: Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's statement descriptor prefix to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement. If the account has no prefix value, the suffix is concatenated to the account's statement descriptor.

charges.name: status
charges.comment: The status of the payment is either succeeded, pending, or failed.

charges.name: transfer_group
charges.comment: A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the Connect documentation for details.

charges.name: transfer_id
charges.comment: ID of the transfer to the destination account (only applicable if the charge was created using the destination parameter).

disputes.name: id
disputes.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

disputes.name: amount
disputes.comment: Disputed amount. Usually the amount of the charge, but it can differ (usually because of currency fluctuation or because only part of the order is disputed).

disputes.name: batch_timestamp
disputes.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

disputes.name: charge_id
disputes.comment: ID of the charge that's disputed.

disputes.name: created
disputes.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

disputes.name: currency
disputes.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

disputes.name: evidence_access_activity_log
disputes.comment: Any server or activity logs showing proof that the customer accessed or downloaded the purchased digital product. This information should include IP addresses, corresponding timestamps, and any detailed recorded activity.

disputes.name: evidence_billing_address
disputes.comment: The billing address provided by the customer.

disputes.name: evidence_cancellation_policy_disclosure
disputes.comment: An explanation of how and when the customer was shown your refund policy prior to purchase.

disputes.name: evidence_cancellation_policy_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Your subscription cancellation policy, as shown to the customer.

disputes.name: evidence_cancellation_rebuttal
disputes.comment: A justification for why the customer's subscription was not canceled.

disputes.name: evidence_customer_communication_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Any communication with the customer that you feel is relevant to your case. Examples include emails proving that the customer received the product or service, or demonstrating their use of or satisfaction with the product or service.

disputes.name: evidence_customer_email_address
disputes.comment: The email address of the customer.

disputes.name: evidence_customer_name
disputes.comment: The name of the customer.

disputes.name: evidence_customer_purchase_ip
disputes.comment: The IP address that the customer used when making the purchase.

disputes.name: evidence_customer_signature_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) A relevant document or contract showing the customer's signature.

disputes.name: evidence_details_due_by
disputes.comment: Date by which evidence must be submitted in order to successfully challenge dispute. Will be 0 if the customer's bank or credit card company doesn't allow a response for this particular dispute.

disputes.name: evidence_details_has_evidence
disputes.comment: Whether evidence has been staged for this dispute.

disputes.name: evidence_details_past_due
disputes.comment: Whether the last evidence submission was submitted past the due date. Defaults to false if no evidence submissions have occurred. If true, then delivery of the latest evidence is not guaranteed.

disputes.name: evidence_details_submission_count
disputes.comment: The number of times evidence has been submitted. Typically, you may only submit evidence once.

disputes.name: evidence_duplicate_charge_documentation_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Documentation for the prior charge that can uniquely identify the charge, such as a receipt, shipping label, work order, etc. This document should be paired with a similar document from the disputed payment that proves the two payments are separate.

disputes.name: evidence_duplicate_charge_id
disputes.comment: The Stripe ID for the prior charge which appears to be a duplicate of the disputed charge.

disputes.name: evidence_product_description
disputes.comment: A description of the product or service that was sold.

disputes.name: evidence_receipt_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Any receipt or message sent to the customer notifying them of the charge.

disputes.name: evidence_refund_policy_disclosure
disputes.comment: Documentation demonstrating that the customer was shown your refund policy prior to purchase.

disputes.name: evidence_refund_policy_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Your refund policy, as shown to the customer.

disputes.name: evidence_refund_refusal_explanation
disputes.comment: A justification for why the customer is not entitled to a refund.

disputes.name: evidence_service_date
disputes.comment: The date on which the customer received or began receiving the purchased service, in a clear human-readable format.

disputes.name: evidence_service_documentation_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Documentation showing proof that a service was provided to the customer. This could include a copy of a signed contract, work order, or other form of written agreement.

disputes.name: evidence_shipping_address
disputes.comment: The address to which a physical product was shipped. You should try to include as complete address information as possible.

disputes.name: evidence_shipping_carrier
disputes.comment: The delivery service that shipped a physical product, such as Fedex, UPS, USPS, etc. If multiple carriers were used for this purchase, please separate them with commas.

disputes.name: evidence_shipping_date
disputes.comment: The date on which a physical product began its route to the shipping address, in a clear human-readable format.

disputes.name: evidence_shipping_documentation_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Documentation showing proof that a product was shipped to the customer at the same address the customer provided to you. This could include a copy of the shipment receipt, shipping label, etc. It should show the customer's full shipping address, if possible.

disputes.name: evidence_shipping_tracking_number
disputes.comment: The tracking number for a physical product, obtained from the delivery service. If multiple tracking numbers were generated for this purchase, please separate them with commas.

disputes.name: evidence_uncategorized_file_id
disputes.comment: (ID of a file upload) Any additional evidence or statements.

disputes.name: evidence_uncategorized_text
disputes.comment: Any additional evidence or statements.

disputes.name: is_charge_refundable
disputes.comment: If true, it's still possible to refund the disputed payment. After the payment has been fully refunded, no further funds are withdrawn from your Stripe account as a result of this dispute.

disputes.name: network_details_type
disputes.comment: The network type for this dispute. There will be a corresponding hash of details keyed by the value of this field.

disputes.name: network_details_visa_rapid_dispute_resolution
disputes.comment: Whether this dispute was resolved via Visa's Rapid Dispute Resolution process.

disputes.name: network_reason_code
disputes.comment: Network-dependent reason code for the dispute.

disputes.name: partner_processed_at
disputes.comment: The timestamp when the partner processed the dispute.

disputes.name: reason
disputes.comment: Reason given by cardholder for dispute. Possible values are bank_cannot_process, check_returned, credit_not_processed, customer_initiated, debit_not_authorized, duplicate, fraudulent, general, incorrect_account_details, insufficient_funds, noncompliant, product_not_received, product_unacceptable, subscription_canceled, or unrecognized. Learn more about dispute reasons.

disputes.name: status
disputes.comment: The current status of a dispute. Possible values include:warning_needs_response, warning_under_review, warning_closed, needs_response, under_review, won, lost, or prevented.

payment_intents.name: id
payment_intents.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

payment_intents.name: amount
payment_intents.comment: Amount intended to be collected by this PaymentIntent. A positive integer representing how much to charge in the smallest currency unit (e.g., 100 cents to charge $1.00 or 100 to charge ¥100, a zero-decimal currency). The minimum amount is $0.50 US or equivalent in charge currency. The amount value supports up to eight digits (e.g., a value of 99999999 for a USD charge of $999,999.99).

payment_intents.name: amount_capturable
payment_intents.comment: Amount that can be captured from this PaymentIntent.

payment_intents.name: amount_details_discount_amount
payment_intents.comment:
The total discount applied on the transaction represented in the smallest currency unit. An integer greater than 0.

This field is mutually exclusive with the amount_details[line_items][#][discount_amount] field.

payment_intents.name: amount_details_shipping_amount
payment_intents.comment: If a physical good is being shipped, the cost of shipping represented in the smallest currency unit. An integer greater than or equal to 0.

payment_intents.name: amount_details_shipping_from_postal_code
payment_intents.comment: If a physical good is being shipped, the postal code of where it is being shipped from. At most 10 alphanumeric characters long, hyphens and spaces are allowed.

payment_intents.name: amount_details_shipping_to_postal_code
payment_intents.comment: If a physical good is being shipped, the postal code of where it is being shipped to. At most 10 alphanumeric characters long, hyphens and spaces are allowed.

payment_intents.name: amount_details_surcharge_amount
payment_intents.comment: Portion of the amount that corresponds to a surcharge.

payment_intents.name: amount_details_tax_total_tax_amount
payment_intents.comment:
The total amount of tax on the transaction represented in the smallest currency unit. Required for L2 rates. An integer greater than or equal to 0.

This field is mutually exclusive with the amount_details[line_items][#][tax][total_tax_amount] field.

payment_intents.name: amount_details_tip_amount
payment_intents.comment: Portion of the amount that corresponds to a tip.

payment_intents.name: application_fee_amount
payment_intents.comment: The amount of the application fee (if any) that will be requested to be applied to the payment and transferred to the application owner's Stripe account. The amount of the application fee collected will be capped at the total amount captured. For more information, see the PaymentIntents use case for connected accounts.

payment_intents.name: application_id
payment_intents.comment: ID of the Connect application that created the PaymentIntent.

payment_intents.name: batch_timestamp
payment_intents.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

payment_intents.name: canceled_at
payment_intents.comment: Populated when status is canceled, this is the time at which the PaymentIntent was canceled. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

payment_intents.name: cancellation_reason
payment_intents.comment: Reason for cancellation of this PaymentIntent, either user-provided (duplicate, fraudulent, requested_by_customer, or abandoned) or generated by Stripe internally (failed_invoice, void_invoice, automatic, or expired).

payment_intents.name: capture_method
payment_intents.comment: Controls when the funds will be captured from the customer's account.

payment_intents.name: card_request_three_d_secure
payment_intents.comment: We strongly recommend that you rely on our SCA Engine to automatically prompt your customers for authentication based on risk level and other requirements. However, if you wish to request 3D Secure based on logic from your own fraud engine, provide this option. If not provided, this value defaults to automatic. Read our guide on manually requesting 3D Secure for more information on how this configuration interacts with Radar and our SCA Engine.

payment_intents.name: confirmation_method
payment_intents.comment: Describes whether we can confirm this PaymentIntent automatically, or if it requires customer action to confirm the payment.

payment_intents.name: created
payment_intents.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

payment_intents.name: currency
payment_intents.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

payment_intents.name: customer_id
payment_intents.comment:
ID of the Customer this PaymentIntent belongs to, if one exists.

Payment methods attached to other Customers cannot be used with this PaymentIntent.

If setup_future_usage is set and this PaymentIntent's payment method is not card_present, then the payment method attaches to the Customer after the PaymentIntent has been confirmed and any required actions from the user are complete. If the payment method is card_present and isn't a digital wallet, then a generated_card payment method representing the card is created and attached to the Customer instead.

payment_intents.name: description
payment_intents.comment: An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.

payment_intents.name: invoice_id
payment_intents.comment: ID of the invoice that created this PaymentIntent, if it exists.

payment_intents.name: last_payment_error_charge
payment_intents.comment: For card errors, the ID of the failed charge.

payment_intents.name: last_payment_error_source
payment_intents.comment: The source object for errors returned on a request involving a source.

payment_intents.name: last_payment_error_type
payment_intents.comment: The type of error returned. One of api_error, card_error, idempotency_error, or invalid_request_error

payment_intents.name: managed_payments_enabled
payment_intents.comment: Whether Managed Payments is enabled for this payment intent.

payment_intents.name: on_behalf_of_id
payment_intents.comment: You can specify the settlement merchant as the connected account using the on_behalf_of attribute on the charge. See the PaymentIntents use case for connected accounts for details.

payment_intents.name: payment_details_customer_reference
payment_intents.comment:
A unique value to identify the customer. This field is available only for card payments.

This field is truncated to 25 alphanumeric characters, excluding spaces, before being sent to card networks.

payment_intents.name: payment_details_order_reference
payment_intents.comment:
A unique value assigned by the business to identify the transaction. Required for L2 and L3 rates.

For Cards, this field is truncated to 25 alphanumeric characters, excluding spaces, before being sent to card networks. For Klarna, this field is truncated to 255 characters and is visible to customers when they view the order in the Klarna app.

payment_intents.name: payment_method_id
payment_intents.comment: ID of the payment method used in this PaymentIntent.

payment_intents.name: payment_method_types
payment_intents.comment: The list of payment method types (e.g. card) that this PaymentIntent is allowed to use. A comprehensive list of valid payment method types can be found here.

payment_intents.name: presentment_amount
payment_intents.comment: Amount intended to be collected by this payment, denominated in presentment_currency.

payment_intents.name: presentment_currency
payment_intents.comment: Currency presented to the customer during payment.

payment_intents.name: receipt_email
payment_intents.comment: Email address that the receipt for the resulting payment will be sent to. If receipt_email is specified for a payment in live mode, a receipt will be sent regardless of your email settings.

payment_intents.name: review_id
payment_intents.comment: ID of the review associated with this PaymentIntent, if any.

payment_intents.name: setup_future_usage
payment_intents.comment:
Indicates that you intend to make future payments with this PaymentIntent's payment method.

If you provide a Customer with the PaymentIntent, you can use this parameter to attach the payment method to the Customer after the PaymentIntent is confirmed and the customer completes any required actions. If you don't provide a Customer, you can still attach the payment method to a Customer after the transaction completes.

If the payment method is card_present and isn't a digital wallet, Stripe creates and attaches a generated_card payment method representing the card to the Customer instead.

When processing card payments, Stripe uses setup_future_usage to help you comply with regional legislation and network rules, such as SCA.

payment_intents.name: statement_descriptor
payment_intents.comment:
Text that appears on the customer's statement as the statement descriptor for a non-card charge. This value overrides the account's default statement descriptor. For information about requirements, including the 22-character limit, see the Statement Descriptor docs.

Setting this value for a card charge returns an error. For card charges, set the statement_descriptor_suffix instead.

payment_intents.name: statement_descriptor_suffix
payment_intents.comment: Provides information about a card charge. Concatenated to the account's statement descriptor prefix to form the complete statement descriptor that appears on the customer's statement.

payment_intents.name: status
payment_intents.comment: Status of this PaymentIntent, one of requires_payment_method, requires_confirmation, requires_action, processing, requires_capture, canceled, or succeeded. Read more about each PaymentIntent status.

payment_method_details.name: ach_debit_account_holder_type
payment_method_details.comment: Type of entity that holds the account. This can be either individual or company.

payment_method_details.name: ach_debit_bank_name
payment_method_details.comment: Name of the bank associated with the bank account.

payment_method_details.name: ach_debit_country
payment_method_details.comment: Two-letter ISO code representing the country the bank account is located in.

payment_method_details.name: ach_debit_fingerprint
payment_method_details.comment: Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.

payment_method_details.name: ach_debit_last4
payment_method_details.comment: Last four digits of the bank account number.

payment_method_details.name: ach_debit_routing_number
payment_method_details.comment: Routing transit number of the bank account.

payment_method_details.name: acss_debit_institution_number
payment_method_details.comment: Institution number of the bank account

payment_method_details.name: acss_debit_transit_number
payment_method_details.comment: Transit number of the bank account.

payment_method_details.name: alipay_fingerprint
payment_method_details.comment: Uniquely identifies this particular Alipay account. You can use this attribute to check whether two Alipay accounts are the same.

payment_method_details.name: alipay_transaction_id
payment_method_details.comment: Transaction ID of this particular Alipay transaction.

payment_method_details.name: au_becs_debit_bsb_number
payment_method_details.comment: Bank-State-Branch number of the bank account.

payment_method_details.name: au_becs_debit_fingerprint
payment_method_details.comment: Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.

payment_method_details.name: au_becs_debit_last4
payment_method_details.comment: Last four digits of the bank account number.

payment_method_details.name: au_becs_debit_mandate_id
payment_method_details.comment: ID of the mandate used to make this payment.

payment_method_details.name: bacs_debit_fingerprint
payment_method_details.comment: Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.

payment_method_details.name: bacs_debit_last4
payment_method_details.comment: Last four digits of the bank account number.

payment_method_details.name: bacs_debit_mandate_id
payment_method_details.comment: ID of the mandate used to make this payment.

payment_method_details.name: bacs_debit_sort_code
payment_method_details.comment: Sort code of the bank account. (e.g., 10-20-30)

payment_method_details.name: batch_timestamp
payment_method_details.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

payment_method_details.name: bizum_buyer_id
payment_method_details.comment: A unique identifier for the buyer as determined by the local payment processor.

payment_method_details.name: bizum_transaction_id
payment_method_details.comment: The Bizum transaction ID associated with this payment.

payment_method_details.name: boleto_expires_at
payment_method_details.comment: Boleto Expiration Timestamp (UTC)

payment_method_details.name: boleto_number
payment_method_details.comment: Boleto Number

payment_method_details.name: card_3ds_authenticated
payment_method_details.comment: Whether or not authentication was performed. 3D Secure will succeed without authentication when the card is not enrolled.

payment_method_details.name: card_3ds_succeeded
payment_method_details.comment: Whether or not 3D Secure succeeded.

payment_method_details.name: card_3ds_version
payment_method_details.comment: The version of 3D Secure that was used

payment_method_details.name: card_address_line1_check
payment_method_details.comment: If a address line1 was provided, results of the check, one of pass, fail, unavailable, or unchecked.

payment_method_details.name: card_address_postal_code_check
payment_method_details.comment: If a address postal code was provided, results of the check, one of pass, fail, unavailable, or unchecked.

payment_method_details.name: card_amount_authorized
payment_method_details.comment: The authorized amount

payment_method_details.name: card_authorization_code
payment_method_details.comment: Authorization code on the charge.

payment_method_details.name: card_brand
payment_method_details.comment: Card brand. Can be amex, cartes_bancaires, diners, discover, eftpos_au, jcb, link, mastercard, unionpay, visa or unknown.

payment_method_details.name: card_brand_product
payment_method_details.comment: The product code that identifies the specific program or product associated with a card.

payment_method_details.name: card_country
payment_method_details.comment: Two-letter ISO code representing the country of the card. You could use this attribute to get a sense of the international breakdown of cards you've collected.

payment_method_details.name: card_cvc_check
payment_method_details.comment: If a CVC was provided, results of the check, one of pass, fail, unavailable, or unchecked.

payment_method_details.name: card_exp_month
payment_method_details.comment: Two-digit number representing the card's expiration month.

payment_method_details.name: card_exp_year
payment_method_details.comment: Four-digit number representing the card's expiration year.

payment_method_details.name: card_fingerprint
payment_method_details.comment:
Uniquely identifies this particular card number. You can use this attribute to check whether two customers who’ve signed up with you are using the same card number, for example. For payment methods that tokenize card information (Apple Pay, Google Pay), the tokenized number might be provided instead of the underlying card number.

As of May 1, 2021, card fingerprint in India for Connect changed to allow two fingerprints for the same card---one for India and one for the rest of the world.

payment_method_details.name: card_funding
payment_method_details.comment: Card funding type. Can be credit, debit, prepaid, or unknown.

payment_method_details.name: card_generated_card
payment_method_details.comment: ID of a card PaymentMethod generated from the card_present PaymentMethod that may be attached to a Customer for future transactions. Only present if it was possible to generate a card PaymentMethod.

payment_method_details.name: card_iin
payment_method_details.comment: Issuer identification number of the card.

payment_method_details.name: card_installments_plan_count
payment_method_details.comment: For fixed_count installment plans, this is the number of installment payments your customer will make to their credit card.

payment_method_details.name: card_installments_plan_interval
payment_method_details.comment: For fixed_count installment plans, this is the interval between installment payments your customer will make to their credit card. One of month.

payment_method_details.name: card_installments_plan_type
payment_method_details.comment: Type of installment plan, one of fixed_count, bonus, or revolving.

payment_method_details.name: card_last4
payment_method_details.comment: The last four digits of the card.

payment_method_details.name: card_mandate
payment_method_details.comment: ID of the mandate used to make this payment or created by it.

payment_method_details.name: card_moto
payment_method_details.comment: True if this payment was marked as MOTO and out of scope for SCA.

payment_method_details.name: card_network
payment_method_details.comment: Identifies which network this charge was processed on. Can be amex, cartes_bancaires, diners, discover, eftpos_au, interac, jcb, link, mastercard, unionpay, visa, or unknown.

payment_method_details.name: card_network_token_used
payment_method_details.comment: Indicates if Stripe used a network token, either user provided or Stripe managed when processing the transaction

payment_method_details.name: card_network_transaction_id
payment_method_details.comment: This is used by the financial networks to identify a transaction. Visa calls this the Transaction ID, Mastercard calls this the Trace ID, and American Express calls this the Acquirer Reference Data. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.

payment_method_details.name: card_present_dynamic_currency_conversion_cardholder_rate
payment_method_details.comment: Exchange rate received by the cardholder, including markup.

payment_method_details.name: card_present_dynamic_currency_conversion_markup_percent
payment_method_details.comment: Markup percentage added to the transaction_fx_rate to get the cardholder_rate.

payment_method_details.name: card_present_dynamic_currency_conversion_original_amount
payment_method_details.comment: Amount in the original currency before conversion, expressed in minor units.

payment_method_details.name: card_present_dynamic_currency_conversion_original_currency
payment_method_details.comment: Original currency before conversion.

payment_method_details.name: card_present_dynamic_currency_conversion_status
payment_method_details.comment: Whether dynamic currency conversion was performed on this transaction. This can be either enabled or disabled.

payment_method_details.name: card_present_dynamic_currency_conversion_transaction_fx_rate
payment_method_details.comment: Exchange rate applied to the transaction, excluding markup.

payment_method_details.name: card_read_method
payment_method_details.comment: How card details were read in this transaction.

payment_method_details.name: card_regulated_status
payment_method_details.comment: Status of a card based on the card issuer.

payment_method_details.name: card_transaction_link_id
payment_method_details.comment: Transaction Link ID (TLID) is a unique identifier for a transaction. This is used by some card networks, such as Mastercard, for transaction linking, in addition to Network Transaction IDs. This value will be present if it is returned by the financial network in the authorization response, and null otherwise.

payment_method_details.name: card_wallet_apple_pay_type
payment_method_details.comment: Apple Pay type. Can be apple_pay, apple_pay_later or unknown.

payment_method_details.name: card_wallet_type
payment_method_details.comment: The type of the card wallet

payment_method_details.name: cashapp_buyer_id
payment_method_details.comment: A unique and immutable identifier assigned by Cash App to every buyer.

payment_method_details.name: cashapp_cashtag
payment_method_details.comment: A public identifier for buyers using Cash App.

payment_method_details.name: cashapp_transaction_id
payment_method_details.comment: A unique and immutable identifier of payments assigned by Cash App

payment_method_details.name: sepa_debit_fingerprint
payment_method_details.comment: Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.

payment_method_details.name: sepa_debit_last4
payment_method_details.comment: Last four digits of the bank account number.

payment_method_details.name: sepa_debit_mandate_id
payment_method_details.comment: ID of the mandate used to make this payment.

refunds.name: balance_transaction_id
refunds.comment: Balance transaction that describes the impact on your account balance.

refunds.name: batch_timestamp
refunds.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

refunds.name: charge_id
refunds.comment: ID of the charge that's refunded.

refunds.name: created
refunds.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

refunds.name: currency
refunds.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

refunds.name: failure_balance_transaction_id
refunds.comment: After the refund fails, this balance transaction describes the adjustment made on your account balance that reverses the initial balance transaction.

refunds.name: failure_reason
refunds.comment: Provides the reason for the refund failure. Possible values are: lost_or_stolen_card, expired_or_canceled_card, charge_for_pending_refund_disputed, insufficient_funds, declined, merchant_request, or unknown.

refunds.name: reason
refunds.comment: Reason for the refund, which is either user-provided (duplicate, fraudulent, or requested_by_customer) or generated by Stripe internally (expired_uncaptured_charge).

refunds.name: receipt_number
refunds.comment: This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this refund.

refunds.name: refund_description
refunds.comment: An arbitrary string attached to the object. You can use this for displaying to users (available on non-card refunds only).

refunds.name: refund_payment_intent
refunds.comment: ID of the PaymentIntent that's refunded.

refunds.name: refund_transfer_reversal_id
refunds.comment: This refers to the transfer reversal object if the accompanying transfer reverses. This is only applicable if the charge was created using the destination parameter.

refunds.name: source_transfer_reversal_id
refunds.comment: The transfer reversal that's associated with the refund. Only present if the charge came from another Stripe account.

refunds.name: status
refunds.comment: Status of the refund. This can be pending, requires_action, succeeded, failed, or canceled. Learn more about failed refunds.

transfers.name: id
transfers.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

transfers.name: amount
transfers.comment: Amount (in cents) to be transferred to your bank account.

transfers.name: amount_reversed
transfers.comment: Amount in cents reversed (can be less than the amount attribute on the transfer if a partial reversal was issued). This field applies to Connect transfer reversals only and differs from the reversed_by and original_payout fields, which link payout reversals.

transfers.name: application_fee_amount
transfers.comment: The amount of the application fee (if any) requested for the payout.

transfers.name: application_fee_id
transfers.comment: The application fee (if any). See the Connect documentation for details.

transfers.name: automatic
transfers.comment: Returns true if the payout was created by an automated payout schedule, and false if it was requested manually.

transfers.name: balance_transaction_id
transfers.comment: Balance transaction that describes the impact of this transfer on your account balance.

transfers.name: batch_timestamp
transfers.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

transfers.name: created
transfers.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

transfers.name: currency
transfers.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

transfers.name: date
transfers.comment: Date the transfer is scheduled to arrive in the bank. This factors in delays like weekends or bank holidays.

transfers.name: destination_id
transfers.comment: ID of the bank account, card, or Stripe account the transfer was sent to.

transfers.name: destination_payment_id
transfers.comment: If the destination is a Stripe account, this will be the ID of the payment that the destination account received for the transfer.

transfers.name: failure_code
transfers.comment: Error code explaining reason for transfer failure if available. See Types of transfer failures for a list of failure codes.

transfers.name: failure_message
transfers.comment: Message to user further explaining reason for transfer failure if available.

transfers.name: original_payout
transfers.comment: If the payout reverses another, this is the ID of the original payout. This field links a reversing payout back to the payout it reversed and differs from the reversed Boolean and amount_reversed fields, which apply to Connect transfer reversals only.

transfers.name: payout_method
transfers.comment: ID of the v2 FinancialAccount the funds were sent to.

transfers.name: reversed
transfers.comment: Whether the transfer has been fully reversed. If the transfer is only partially reversed, this attribute will still be false. This field applies to Connect transfer reversals only and differs from the reversed_by and original_payout fields, which link payout reversals.

transfers.name: reversed_by
transfers.comment: If the payout reverses, this is the ID of the payout that reverses this payout. This field links payout reversals to their originals and differs from the reversed Boolean and amount_reversed fields, which apply to Connect transfer reversals only.

transfers.name: source_transaction_id
transfers.comment: ID of the charge (or other transaction) that was used to fund the transfer. If null, the transfer was funded from the available balance.

transfers.name: source_type
transfers.comment: The source balance this transfer came from. One of card, fpx, or bank_account.

transfers.name: statement_descriptor
transfers.comment: Extra information about a transfer to be displayed on the user's bank statement.

transfers.name: transfer_group
transfers.comment: A string that identifies this transaction as part of a group. See the Connect documentation for details.

transfers.name: type
transfers.comment: Can be card, bank_account, or stripe_account.

customers.name: account_balance

customers.name: address_city

customers.name: address_country

customers.comment: Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.

customers.name: address_line2
customers.comment: Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

customers.name: address_postal_code
customers.comment: ZIP or postal code.

customers.name: address_state
customers.comment: State, county, province, or region (ISO 3166-2).

customers.name: balance
customers.comment: The current balance, if any, that's stored on the customer. If negative, the customer has credit to apply to their next invoice. If positive, the customer has an amount owed that's added to their next invoice. The balance only considers amounts that Stripe hasn't successfully applied to any invoice. It doesn't reflect unpaid invoices. This balance is only taken into account after invoices finalize.

customers.name: batch_timestamp
customers.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

customers.name: business_name
customers.comment: The customer's business name.

customers.name: created
customers.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

customers.name: currency
customers.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

customers.name: customer_account_id
customers.comment: The ID of a related account that has the customer configuration. This ID can be used in any v1 API that accepts a customer_account parameter.

customers.name: default_source_id
customers.comment:
ID of the default payment source for the customer.

If you use payment methods created through the PaymentMethods API, see the invoice_settings.default_payment_method field instead.

customers.name: delinquent
customers.comment:
Tracks the most recent state change on any invoice belonging to the customer. Paying an invoice or marking it uncollectible via the API will set this field to false. An automatic payment failure or passing the invoice.due_date will set this field to true.

If an invoice becomes uncollectible by dunning, delinquent doesn't reset to false.

If you care whether the customer has paid their most recent subscription invoice, use subscription.status instead. Paying or marking uncollectible any customer invoice regardless of whether it is the latest invoice for a subscription will always set this field to false.

customers.name: description
customers.comment: An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.

customers.name: discount_checkout_session
customers.comment: The Checkout session that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular session in payment mode. Not present for subscription mode.

customers.name: discount_coupon_id
customers.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

customers.name: discount_customer_id
customers.comment: The ID of the customer associated with this discount.

customers.name: discount_end
customers.comment: If the coupon has a duration of repeating, the date that this discount will end. If the coupon has a duration of once or forever, this attribute will be null.

customers.name: discount_invoice
customers.comment: The invoice that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice.

customers.name: discount_invoice_item
customers.comment: The invoice item id (or invoice line item id for invoice line items of type='subscription') that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice item or invoice line item.

customers.name: discount_promotion_code_id
customers.comment: The promotion code applied to create this discount.

customers.name: discount_schedule_id
customers.comment: The subscription schedule that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription schedule.

customers.name: discount_start
customers.comment: Date that the coupon was applied.

customers.name: discount_subscription
customers.comment: The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.

customers.name: discount_subscription_item
customers.comment: The subscription item that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription item.

customers.name: email
customers.comment: The customer's email address.

customers.name: individual_name
customers.comment: The customer's individual name.

customers.name: invoice_credit_balance
customers.comment: The current multi-currency balances, if any, that's stored on the customer. If positive in a currency, the customer has a credit to apply to their next invoice denominated in that currency. If negative, the customer has an amount owed that's added to their next invoice denominated in that currency. These balances don't apply to unpaid invoices. They solely track amounts that Stripe hasn't successfully applied to any invoice. Stripe only applies a balance in a specific currency to an invoice after that invoice (which is in the same currency) finalizes.

customers.name: invoice_settings_default_payment_method_id
customers.comment: ID of a payment method that's attached to the customer, to be used as the customer's default payment method for subscriptions and invoices.

customers.name: name
customers.comment: The customer's full name or business name.

customers.name: phone
customers.comment: The customer's phone number.

customers.name: preferred_locales
customers.comment: The customer's preferred locales (languages), ordered by preference.

customers.name: shipping_address_city
customers.comment: City, district, suburb, town, or village.

customers.name: shipping_address_country
customers.comment: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

customers.name: shipping_address_line1
customers.comment: Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.

customers.name: shipping_address_line2
customers.comment: Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

customers.name: shipping_address_postal_code
customers.comment: ZIP or postal code.

customers.name: shipping_address_state
customers.comment: State, county, province, or region (ISO 3166-2).

customers.name: shipping_name
customers.comment: Customer name.

customers.name: shipping_phone
customers.comment: Customer phone (including extension).

customers.name: sources_data_id
customers.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

customers.name: tax_exempt
customers.comment: Describes the customer's tax exemption status, which is none, exempt, or reverse. When set to reverse, invoice and receipt PDFs include the following text: "Reverse charge".

customers.name: tax_info_tax_id
customers.comment: The customer's tax ID number.

customers.name: tax_info_type
customers.comment: The type of ID number.

customers.name: tax_ip_address
customers.comment: A recent IP address of the customer used for tax reporting and tax location inference.

invoice_line_items.name: amount
invoice_line_items.comment: The amount, in cents.

invoice_line_items.name: currency

invoice_line_items.comment: The globally unique id for this invoice line item.

invoice_line_items.name: invoice_item_id
invoice_line_items.comment: The ID of the invoice item associated with this line item if any.

invoice_line_items.name: line_item_parent_id
invoice_line_items.comment: The parent object id derived from parent details for this line item.

invoice_line_items.name: line_item_parent_type
invoice_line_items.comment: The type of parent that generated this line item. Mirrors parent.type from the API.

invoice_line_items.name: period_end
invoice_line_items.comment: The end of the period, which must be greater than or equal to the start. This value is inclusive.

invoice_line_items.name: period_start
invoice_line_items.comment: The start of the period. This value is inclusive.

invoice_line_items.name: plan_id
invoice_line_items.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

invoice_line_items.name: price_id

invoice_line_items.name: proration

invoice_line_items.name: proration_details_credited_items_invoice
invoice_line_items.comment: Invoice containing the credited invoice line items

invoice_line_items.name: proration_details_credited_items_invoice_line_items
invoice_line_items.comment: Credited invoice line items
