For the line item's full-precision decimal quantity, use quantity_decimal. This field will be deprecated in favor of quantity_decimal in a future version. If the line item is a proration or subscription, the quantity of the subscription that the proration was computed for.

invoice_line_items.name: quantity_decimal
invoice_line_items.comment: Non-negative decimal with at most 12 decimal places. The quantity of units for the line item.

invoice_line_items.name: source_id
invoice_line_items.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

invoice_line_items.name: source_type
invoice_line_items.comment: A string identifying the type of the source of this line item, either an invoiceitem or a subscription.

invoice_line_items.name: subscription_item_id
invoice_line_items.comment: The subscription item that generated this line item. Left empty if the line item is not an explicit result of a subscription.

invoice_line_items.name: total_discount
invoice_line_items.comment: The sum total of the top- and item-level discounts applied to this line item.

invoice_line_items.name: total_exclusive_tax
invoice_line_items.comment: The sum total of the exclusive taxes applied to this line item.

invoices.name: id
invoices.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

invoices.name: amount_due
invoices.comment: Final amount due at this time for this invoice. If the invoice's total is smaller than the minimum charge amount, for example, or if there is account credit that can be applied to the invoice, the amount_due may be 0. If there is a positive starting_balance for the invoice (the customer owes money), the amount_due will also take that into account. The charge that gets generated for the invoice will be for the amount specified in amount_due.

invoices.name: amount_paid
invoices.comment: The amount, in cents, that was paid.

invoices.name: amount_remaining
invoices.comment: The difference between amount_due and amount_paid, in cents.

invoices.name: amount_shipping
invoices.comment: This is the sum of all the shipping amounts.

invoices.name: application_id
invoices.comment: ID of the Connect Application that created the invoice.

invoices.name: attempt_count
invoices.comment: Number of payment attempts made for this invoice, from the perspective of the payment retry schedule. Any payment attempt counts as the first attempt, and subsequently only automatic retries increment the attempt count. In other words, manual payment attempts after the first attempt do not affect the retry schedule. If a failure is returned with a non-retryable return code, the invoice can no longer be retried unless a new payment method is obtained. Retries will continue to be scheduled, and attempt_count will continue to increment, but retries will only be executed if a new payment method is obtained.

invoices.name: attempted
invoices.comment: Whether an attempt has been made to pay the invoice. An invoice is not attempted until 1 hour after the invoice.created webhook, for example, so you might not want to display that invoice as unpaid to your users.

invoices.name: auto_advance
invoices.comment: Controls whether Stripe performs automatic collection of the invoice. If false, the invoice's state doesn't automatically advance without an explicit action.

invoices.name: automatic_tax_enabled
invoices.comment: Whether Stripe automatically computes tax on this invoice. Note that incompatible invoice items (invoice items with manually specified tax rates, negative amounts, or tax_behavior=unspecified) cannot be added to automatic tax invoices.

invoices.name: automatic_tax_provider
invoices.comment: The tax provider powering automatic tax.

invoices.name: automatic_tax_status
invoices.comment: The status of the most recent automated tax calculation for this invoice.

invoices.name: batch_timestamp
invoices.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

invoices.name: billing_reason
invoices.comment:
Indicates the reason why the invoice was created.

manual: Unrelated to a subscription, for example, created via the invoice editor.
subscription: No longer in use. Applies to subscriptions from before May 2018 where no distinction was made between updates, cycles, and thresholds.
subscription_create: A new subscription was created.
subscription_cycle: A subscription advanced into a new period.
subscription_threshold: A subscription reached a billing threshold.
subscription_update: A subscription was updated.
upcoming: Reserved for upcoming invoices created through the Create Preview Invoice API or when an invoice.upcoming event is generated for an upcoming invoice on a subscription.

invoices.name: charge_id
invoices.comment: ID of the latest charge generated for this invoice, if any.

invoices.name: currency
invoices.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

invoices.name: customer_address_city
invoices.comment: City, district, suburb, town, or village.

invoices.name: customer_address_country
invoices.comment: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

invoices.name: customer_address_line1
invoices.comment: Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.

invoices.name: customer_address_line2
invoices.comment: Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

invoices.name: customer_address_postal_code
invoices.comment: ZIP or postal code.

invoices.name: customer_address_state
invoices.comment: State, county, province, or region (ISO 3166-2).

invoices.name: customer_email
invoices.comment: The customer's email. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal customer.email. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated.

invoices.name: customer_id
invoices.comment: The ID of the customer to bill.

invoices.name: customer_name
invoices.comment: The customer's name. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal customer.name. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated.

invoices.name: customer_phone
invoices.comment: The customer's phone number. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal customer.phone. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated.

invoices.name: customer_shipping_address_city
invoices.comment: City, district, suburb, town, or village.

invoices.name: customer_shipping_address_country
invoices.comment: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

invoices.name: customer_shipping_address_line1
invoices.comment: Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.

invoices.name: customer_shipping_address_line2
invoices.comment: Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

invoices.name: customer_shipping_address_postal_code
invoices.comment: ZIP or postal code.

invoices.name: customer_shipping_address_state
invoices.comment: State, county, province, or region (ISO 3166-2).

invoices.name: customer_shipping_name
invoices.comment: Customer name.

invoices.name: customer_shipping_phone
invoices.comment: Customer phone (including extension).

invoices.name: customer_tax_exempt
invoices.comment: The customer's tax exempt status. Until the invoice is finalized, this field will equal customer.tax_exempt. Once the invoice is finalized, this field will no longer be updated.

invoices.name: date
invoices.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

invoices.name: default_payment_method_id
invoices.comment: ID of the default payment method for the invoice. It must belong to the customer associated with the invoice. If not set, defaults to the subscription's default payment method, if any, or to the default payment method in the customer's invoice settings.

invoices.name: description
invoices.comment: An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users. Referenced as 'memo' in the Dashboard.

invoices.name: discount_checkout_session
invoices.comment: The Checkout session that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular session in payment mode. Not present for subscription mode.

invoices.name: discount_coupon_id
invoices.comment: Unique identifier for the object.

invoices.name: discount_customer_id
invoices.comment: The ID of the customer associated with this discount.

invoices.name: discount_end
invoices.comment: If the coupon has a duration of repeating, the date that this discount will end. If the coupon has a duration of once or forever, this attribute will be null.

invoices.name: discount_invoice
invoices.comment: The invoice that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice.

invoices.name: discount_invoice_item
invoices.comment: The invoice item id (or invoice line item id for invoice line items of type='subscription') that the discount's coupon was applied to, if it was applied directly to a particular invoice item or invoice line item.

invoices.name: discount_promotion_code_id
invoices.comment: The promotion code applied to create this discount.

invoices.name: discount_schedule_id
invoices.comment: The subscription schedule that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription schedule.

invoices.name: discount_start
invoices.comment: Date that the coupon was applied.

invoices.name: discount_subscription
invoices.comment: The subscription that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription.

invoices.name: discount_subscription_item
invoices.comment: The subscription item that this coupon is applied to, if it is applied to a particular subscription item.

invoices.name: discounts
invoices.comment: The discounts applied to the invoice. Line item discounts are applied before invoice discounts. Use expand[]=discounts to expand each discount.

invoices.name: due_date
invoices.comment: The date on which payment for this invoice is due. This value will be null for invoices where collection_method=charge_automatically.

invoices.name: effective_at
invoices.comment: The date when this invoice is in effect. Same as finalized_at unless overwritten. When defined, this value replaces the system-generated 'Date of issue' printed on the invoice PDF and receipt.

invoices.name: footer
invoices.comment: Footer displayed on the invoice.

invoices.name: next_payment_attempt
invoices.comment: The time at which payment will next be attempted. This value will be null for invoices where collection_method=send_invoice.

invoices.name: number
invoices.comment: A unique, identifying string that appears on emails sent to the customer for this invoice. This starts with the customer's unique invoice_prefix if it is specified.

invoices.name: on_behalf_of_id
invoices.comment: The account (if any) for which the funds of the invoice payment are intended. If set, the invoice will be presented with the branding and support information of the specified account. See the Invoices with Connect documentation for details.

invoices.name: paid
invoices.comment: Whether payment was successfully collected for this invoice. An invoice can be paid (most commonly) with a charge or with credit from the customer's account balance.

invoices.name: paid_out_of_band
invoices.comment: Returns true if the invoice was manually marked paid, returns false if the invoice hasn't been paid yet or was paid on Stripe.

invoices.name: parent_id
invoices.comment: The ID of the parent that generated the invoice.

invoices.name: parent_type
invoices.comment: The parent type of the invoice. Possible values: billing_cadence, subscription, quote, schedule.

invoices.name: period_end
invoices.comment: The latest timestamp at which invoice items can be associated with this invoice. Use the line item period to get the service period for each price.

invoices.name: period_start
invoices.comment: The earliest timestamp at which invoice items can be associated with this invoice. Use the line item period to get the service period for each price.

invoices.name: post_payment_credit_notes_amount
invoices.comment: Total amount of all post-payment credit notes issued for this invoice.

invoices.name: pre_payment_credit_notes_amount
invoices.comment: Total amount of all pre-payment credit notes issued for this invoice.

invoices.name: quote_id
invoices.comment: The quote this invoice was generated from.

invoices.name: receipt_number
invoices.comment: This is the transaction number that appears on email receipts sent for this invoice.

invoices.name: shipping_cost_amount_subtotal
invoices.comment: Total shipping cost before any taxes are applied.

invoices.name: shipping_cost_amount_tax
invoices.comment: Total tax amount applied due to shipping costs. If no tax was applied, defaults to 0.

invoices.name: shipping_cost_amount_total
invoices.comment: Total shipping cost after taxes are applied.

invoices.name: shipping_cost_shipping_rate_id
invoices.comment: The ID of the ShippingRate for this invoice.

invoices.name: shipping_details_address_city
invoices.comment: City, district, suburb, town, or village.

invoices.name: shipping_details_address_country
invoices.comment: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2).

invoices.name: shipping_details_address_line1
invoices.comment: Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.

invoices.name: shipping_details_address_line2
invoices.comment: Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

invoices.name: shipping_details_address_postal_code
invoices.comment: ZIP or postal code.

invoices.name: shipping_details_address_state
invoices.comment: State, county, province, or region (ISO 3166-2).

invoices.name: shipping_details_name
invoices.comment: Recipient name.

invoices.name: shipping_details_phone
invoices.comment: Recipient phone (including extension).

invoices.name: starting_balance
invoices.comment: Starting customer balance before the invoice is finalized. If the invoice has not been finalized yet, this will be the current customer balance.

invoices.name: statement_descriptor
invoices.comment: Extra information about an invoice for the customer's credit card statement.

invoices.name: status
invoices.comment: The status of the invoice, one of draft, open, paid, uncollectible, or void. Learn more

invoices.name: status_transitions_finalized_at
invoices.comment: The time that the invoice draft was finalized.

invoices.name: status_transitions_marked_uncollectible_at
invoices.comment: The time that the invoice was marked uncollectible.

invoices.name: status_transitions_paid_at
invoices.comment: The time that the invoice was paid.

invoices.name: status_transitions_voided_at
invoices.comment: The time that the invoice was voided.

invoices.name: subscription_id
invoices.comment: The subscription that this invoice was prepared for, if any.

invoices.name: subscription_proration_date
invoices.comment: Only set for upcoming invoices that preview prorations. The time used to calculate prorations.

invoices.name: subtotal
invoices.comment: Total of all subscriptions, invoice items, and prorations on the invoice before any invoice level discount or exclusive tax is applied. Item discounts are already incorporated

invoices.name: tax
invoices.comment: The amount of tax on this invoice. This is the sum of all the tax amounts on this invoice.

invoices.name: tax_percent
invoices.comment: This percentage of the subtotal has been added to the total amount of the invoice, including invoice line items and discounts. This field is inherited from the subscription's tax_percent field, but can be changed before the invoice is paid. This field defaults to null.

invoices.name: total
invoices.comment: Total after discounts and taxes.

invoices.name: transfer_data_amount
invoices.comment: The amount in cents that will be transferred to the destination account when the invoice is paid. By default, the entire amount is transferred to the destination.

invoices.name: transfer_data_destination_id
invoices.comment: The account where funds from the payment will be transferred to upon payment success.

invoices.name: webhooks_delivered_at
invoices.comment: Invoices are automatically paid or sent 1 hour after webhooks are delivered, or until all webhook delivery attempts have been exhausted. This field tracks the time when webhooks for this invoice were successfully delivered. If the invoice had no webhooks to deliver, this will be set while the invoice is being created.

prices.name: id
prices.comment: The ID of the price object.

prices.name: active
prices.comment: Whether the price can be used for new purchases.

prices.name: batch_timestamp
prices.comment: The time in epoch format at which updates to the object were processed through the Stripe Data Pipeline. If the object hasn't changed, the time remains unchanged. This field isn't available in Sigma. It's only available for core API tables, including Connect versions, exported through the Stripe Data Pipeline.

prices.name: billing_scheme
prices.comment: Describes how to compute the price per period. Either per_unit or tiered. per_unit indicates that the fixed amount (specified in unit_amount or unit_amount_decimal) will be charged per unit in quantity (for prices with usage_type=licensed), or per unit of total usage (for prices with usage_type=metered). tiered indicates that the unit pricing will be computed using a tiering strategy as defined using the tiers and tiers_mode attributes.

prices.name: created
prices.comment: Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.

prices.name: currency
prices.comment: Three-letter ISO currency code, in lowercase. Must be a supported currency.

prices.name: custom_unit_amount_default
prices.comment: The starting unit amount which can be updated by the customer.

prices.name: custom_unit_amount_maximum
prices.comment: The maximum unit amount the customer can specify for this item.

prices.name: custom_unit_amount_minimum
prices.comment: The minimum unit amount the customer can specify for this item. Must be at least the minimum charge amount.

prices.name: lookup_key
prices.comment: A lookup key used to retrieve prices dynamically from a static string. This may be up to 200 characters.

prices.name: nickname
prices.comment: A brief description of the price, hidden from customers.

prices.name: product_id
prices.comment: The ID of the product this price is associated with.

prices.name: recurring_aggregate_usage
prices.comment: Specifies a usage aggregation strategy for prices of usage_type=metered. Defaults to sum.

prices.name: recurring_interval
prices.comment: The frequency at which a subscription is billed. One of day, week, month or year.

prices.name: recurring_interval_count
prices.comment: The number of intervals (specified in the interval attribute) between subscription billings. For example, interval=month and interval_count=3 bills every 3 months.

prices.name: recurring_meter_id
prices.comment: The meter tracking the usage of a metered price

prices.name: recurring_trial_period_days
prices.comment: Default number of trial days when subscribing a customer to this price using trial_from_plan=true.

prices.name: recurring_usage_type
prices.comment: Configures how the quantity per period should be determined. Can be either metered or licensed. licensed automatically bills the quantity set when adding it to a subscription. metered aggregates the total usage based on usage records. Defaults to licensed.

prices.name: tax_behavior
prices.comment: Only required if a default tax behavior was not provided in the Stripe Tax settings. Specifies whether the price is considered inclusive of taxes or exclusive of taxes. One of inclusive, exclusive, or unspecified. Once specified as either inclusive or exclusive, it cannot be changed.

prices.name: tiers_mode
prices.comment: Defines if the tiering price should be graduated or volume based. In volume-based tiering, the maximum quantity within a period determines the per unit price. In graduated tiering, pricing can change as the quantity grows.

prices.name: transform_quantity_divide_by
prices.comment: Divide usage by this number.

prices.name: transform_quantity_round
prices.comment: After division, either round the result up or down.

prices.name: type
prices.comment: One of one_time or recurring depending on whether the price is for a one-time purchase or a recurring (subscription) purchase.

prices.name: unit_amount
prices.comment: The unit amount in cents to be charged, represented as a whole integer if possible. Only set if billing_scheme=per_unit.

prices.name: unit_amount_decimal
prices.comment: The unit amount in cents to be charged, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places. Only set if billing_scheme=per_unit.

products.name: type

products.name: unit_label
products.comment: A label that represents units of this product. When set, this will be included in customers' receipts, invoices, Checkout, and the customer portal.

products.name: url

subscriptions.comment: Either charge_automatically, or send_invoice. When sending an invoice, Stripe will email your customer an invoice with payment instructions and mark the subscription as active.

subscriptions.name: status
subscriptions.comment:
Possible values are incomplete, incomplete_expired, trialing, active, past_due, canceled, unpaid, or paused.

For collection_method=charge_automatically a subscription moves into incomplete if the initial payment attempt fails. A subscription in this status can only have metadata and default_source updated. Once the first invoice is paid, the subscription moves into an active status. If the first invoice is not paid within 23 hours, the subscription transitions to incomplete_expired. This is a terminal status, the open invoice will be voided and no further invoices will be generated.

A subscription that is currently in a trial period is trialing and moves to active when the trial period is over.

A subscription can only enter a paused status when a trial ends without a payment method. A paused subscription doesn't generate invoices and can be resumed after your customer adds their payment method. The paused status is different from pausing collection, which still generates invoices and leaves the subscription's status unchanged.

If subscription collection_method=charge_automatically, it becomes past_due when payment is required but cannot be paid (due to failed payment or awaiting additional user actions). Once Stripe has exhausted all payment retry attempts, the subscription will become canceled or unpaid (depending on your subscriptions settings).

If subscription collection_method=send_invoice it becomes past_due when its invoice is not paid by the due date, and canceled or unpaid if it is still not paid by an additional deadline after that. Note that when a subscription has a status of unpaid, no subsequent invoices will be attempted (invoices will be created, but then immediately automatically closed). After receiving updated payment information from a customer, you may choose to reopen and pay their closed invoices.

itemized_fees.comment: One line description of the product feature

itemized_fees.name: feature_name
itemized_fees.comment: The product feature the fee belongs to. For instance, Radar for Fraud Teams - transaction fee.

itemized_fees.name: fee_category
itemized_fees.comment: [Deprecated] Fee category where product feature description maps to. This field is no longer maintained and could have incomplete data. Use the product and suite fields instead.

itemized_fees.name: fee_description
itemized_fees.comment: One line fee description. Use this in place of balance_transaction_description

itemized_fees.name: fee_transaction_created
itemized_fees.comment: Time (in UTC) at which the fee transaction affected your Stripe/Credit balance.

itemized_fees.name: fee_transaction_id
itemized_fees.comment: The id of the fee transaction containing the fee.

itemized_fees.name: incurred_at
itemized_fees.comment: Time (in UTC) at which the fee was incurred, by the date of its originating event.

itemized_fees.name: incurred_by
itemized_fees.comment: The ID of the object that incurred this fee, if any. Use the incurred_by_type field to determine the type of this object.

itemized_fees.name: incurred_by_type
itemized_fees.comment: The object type which the incurred_by references. Matches the object field in the API (charge, refund, invoice, etc).

itemized_fees.name: invoice_number
itemized_fees.comment: The number of the invoice which was sent to invoice the Fees. This field will be null for non-invoiced fees.

itemized_fees.name: platform_id
itemized_fees.comment: Platform account ID

itemized_fees.name: pricing_tier
itemized_fees.comment: The pricing tier at which this fee was assessed.

itemized_fees.name: product
itemized_fees.comment: The product area the fee belongs to. For instance, Radar.

itemized_fees.name: product_feature_description
itemized_fees.comment: [Deprecated] The product and feature description of the fee. This field is no longer maintained and could have incomplete data. Use the feature_name field instead.

itemized_fees.name: settled_at
itemized_fees.comment: The column gives information on when these fees were settled. In case of Invoices, this is the invoice sent date.

itemized_fees.name: settled_via
itemized_fees.comment: This column gives information on how a particular fee was settled. Possible Values are credit, balance, v2_balance, invoice and multiple.

itemized_fees.name: suite
itemized_fees.comment: The product suite the fee belongs to. For instance, Payments.

itemized_fees.name: tax
itemized_fees.comment: Tax of this activity, expressed in major units of the currency.
